title: Two-Stage Controlled → FLUX Bake-off
hypothesis: ControlNet = geometry enforcer; FLUX = realism enhancer. Two-stage is better than either model alone.

test_A.description: FLUX.2 Klein applied directly to front-face RGB (no ControlNet)

wall_geometry.note: Back wall preserved; column at center-right correct.

openings.note: Kitchen archway visible on left; refrigerator depth present.

ceiling.note: Flat white ceiling at correct height.

cabinetry.note: TV unit with floating shelves correctly positioned.

furniture_pos.note: Sofa, coffee table in correct positions.

material_realism.note: Warm walnut wood grain on TV unit and sideboard; concrete floor; linen sofa texture.

lighting_realism.note: Warm directional daylight from left; soft indirect fill; recessed downlights hinted.

texture_richness.note: Strong material differentiation: fabric, wood, concrete, glass.

added_objects.note: Small decorative plant near TV unit (not in source).

test_A.overall: Strong result. FLUX alone on front-face RGB produces excellent photorealism with good geometry fidelity. Geometry preservation is strong because the source (512×512 Blender render at denoise=0 effectively) is already geometrically clean.

test_B.description: SD1.5 + ControlNet Depth only (Stage 1); no FLUX

wall_geometry.note: Wall geometry well preserved; column present.

openings.note: Kitchen area loosely indicated but not clearly open.

cabinetry.note: TV unit and shelf correctly placed.

furniture_pos.note: Sofa and foreground elements in correct positions.

material_realism.note: Flat neutral grey/beige palette. No material differentiation. Looks like Blender render.

lighting_realism.note: Flat ambient illumination. No directionality or depth.

texture_richness.note: Uniform grey surfaces with no texture detail.

photographic_quality.note: Clearly a 3D render output, not a photograph.

test_B.overall: Geometry is well constrained. Material and lighting quality is insufficient for the final product. Stage 1 alone is geometrically correct but not photorealistic.

wall_geometry.note: Back wall and column preserved from Stage 1.

openings.note: Kitchen opening visible; depth into kitchen present.

cabinetry.note: TV unit with shelves maintained; wood shelf element prominent.

furniture_pos.note: Sofa, coffee table, sideboard all correctly positioned.

material_realism.note: Walnut TV unit matches source intent; polished floor; linen sofa fabric; concrete walls.

lighting_realism.note: Warm directional daylight from left; soft shadows; architectural depth.

reflections.note: Polished floor reflections visible; sofa reflected in floor.

texture_richness.note: Strong material differentiation across all surfaces.

photographic_quality.note: Architectural photography appearance. Comparable to Test A.

added_objects.note: Small decorative objects on shelf (not in source). Same category as Test A.

redesigned.note: No architectural redesign. Stage 1 geometry intact.

test_C.overall: Two-stage result combines Stage 1 geometry fidelity with FLUX photorealism. No geometric drift from Stage 1 to Stage 2. All major architectural elements preserved through both stages.

key_comparison_B_vs_C.question: Does FLUX materially improve realism while preserving the geometry established by ControlNet?
key_comparison_B_vs_C.geometry_drift_B_to_C: NONE — all 7 geometry criteria pass in both B and C. Column, TV unit, sofa, camera composition, ceiling, openings all maintained.
key_comparison_B_vs_C.realism_gain: SUBSTANTIAL — all 5 visual quality criteria go from POOR/FAIL in B to EXCELLENT/GOOD in C. FLUX added material texture, directional lighting, floor reflections, and photographic tonal range without touching the geometry.
key_comparison_B_vs_C.hallucination_delta: NEUTRAL — same minor class of small decorative object additions as Test A. Not attributable to ControlNet geometry.

verdict_rationale: Stage 1 (ControlNet) established correct geometry in 12s on RTX 2060 at no API cost. Stage 2 (FLUX) converted the flat CG render into photorealistic architectural photography in 7.2s via Cloudflare. The two-stage architecture produces a result that is visually superior to B (ControlNet alone) across all 5 visual quality dimensions, with zero measurable geometry drift from B to C. Test A (FLUX direct on RGB) is a strong alternative — geometry is also well preserved at denoise=0 — but C is preferred because Stage 1 provides an explicit geometry contract that is guaranteed to survive FLUX's creative realism pass.
recommendation_rationale: ControlNet → FLUX is worth keeping as the new candidate generation architecture. The depth ControlNet acts as a geometry lock that prevents FLUX from redesigning the space during its realism pass. The empirical result confirms the hypothesis. Proceed to multi-face testing if warranted.
stop_condition: Stopping after A/B/C comparison per Phase 0J brief. Do NOT proceed to six-face generation automatically.
